I've implemented toolchain tracking across the Twister test runner. Here's a summary of the changes (all in source files, none in `tests/`):

**`testinstance.py`** — `TestInstance.__init__` now takes `toolchain` after `platform`, stores it as `self.toolchain`, includes it in `self.name` (`platform.name/toolchain/testsuite.name`), and inserts it as a path segment in `build_dir` (`outdir/platform.normalized_name/toolchain/<test_path>`).

**`testsuite.py`** — Initializes `self.integration_toolchains = []`. The existing `load()` (which `setattr`s every YAML key) populates it automatically.

**`testsuite-schema.yaml`** — Added the `integration_toolchains` key as an optional sequence of strings.

**`testplan.py`**
- Imported `product` from `itertools`.
- `apply_filters` now iterates `product(ts.integration_toolchains or [None], platform_scope)`, deriving the toolchain per instance: an explicit integration toolchain wins; else `host`/`llvm` for `posix`/`unit` arches; else the env toolchain (defaulting to `zephyr`). This generates a config per platform×toolchain combination regardless of `--integration`. The existing toolchain filters (`toolchain_allow`/`exclude`, "not supported by toolchain") now operate on the per-instance toolchain.
- Since instances are keyed by `instance.name` (now `platform/toolchain/testsuite`), `add_instances` and the quarantine/filter lookups incorporate the toolchain automatically.
- `load_from_file` reads `ts["toolchain"]` and passes it to the constructor.

**`runner.py`** — Adds `-DZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=<toolchain>` to the CMake command, and appends the toolchain to progress logs (`... elapsed_time <toolchain>` for runs, `build <toolchain>` for build-only).

**`reports.py`** — Serializes `"toolchain": instance.toolchain` into each test-plan suite entry (round-tripped by `load_from_file`).
